edit.statement: Every Liberty ship was built in the United States.
edit.subject: Liberty ship
edit.scope: The 2,710 Liberty ships, Maritime Commission design EC2-S-C1, of the Second World War and the country whose shipyards built them; the British Ocean ships, the Canadian Fort and Park ships and the later Victory ships are other classes. The Boccadasse, joined at Genoa in 1950 from the halves of two wrecked American-built Liberty ships, was built in the United States as hulls. Deleting the rule takes with it the facts that restate it, such as the eighteen American yards of the Emergency Shipbuilding Program and Kaiser's yards building Liberty ships; otherwise they would give the country back.

notes: Mirrors history-replace-0019: deletes the original rule. New members named in the prompt are does-not-know in every world (determinate). Well-known members keep the United States in the world that stores their shipyard by name (Maine or Maryland, then the chain to the country), and are does-not-know in the world that reached the country only through the deleted rule (background beliefs); with the rule gone, the by-name world needs no membership to give way. Four worlds, from two independent storage choices. Verifier: the museum ships are tied to the class by their keepers' names (National Liberty Ship Memorial, Project Liberty Ship), not by any firm fact about the ship, so leaving the class contradicts nothing outside the chain.
